content_sections.title: Notice meaning and form
content_sections.body_text: Use the present simple for a fact or usual action. I/you/we/they live and study; he/she lives and studies. A time phrase such as every day signals a routine. Read the forms, cover them, then say them from memory.

content_sections.title: Read a personal model
content_sections.body_text: Model: ‘I am Minh. I live in Hue. I study English every day. My sister lives in Da Nang.’ Notice which facts are stable and which action is usual. Then replace the names, places, and routine with safe information about you.

content_sections.title: Make final sounds clear
content_sections.body_text: In live /lɪv/, upper teeth touch the lower lip for /v/. In lives /lɪvz/ and studies /ˈstʌdiz/, the last sound /z/ uses the tongue close to the ridge behind the upper teeth. Both sounds buzz. Build the last sound alone, then add the word; do not add a vowel.

content_sections.title: Produce and self-check
content_sections.body_text: Record live, lives, and studies. Replay and check: live and lives each have one beat; studies has two. The final buzz continues briefly; lip plus teeth signals /v/, and tongue near the ridge signals /z/. If a sound is missing or a new beat appears, rebuild sound → word → sentence. Then record four safe personal sentences.
